theory.overview: Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree or BIT) is a data structure for efficient prefix sum queries and point updates. Simpler and more space-efficient than segment tree for prefix sum operations. Supports point update and prefix sum query in $O(\log n)$ time. Range sum query = two prefix sum queries. Used in frequency counting, cumulative sums, and inversion counting. This chapter covers BIT structure, operations, and applications.

sections.title: BIT Structure
sections.content: Array of size n+1 (1-indexed). Each index i stores sum of a range of original array. The range is determined by the lowest set bit of i: i & -i (two's complement). Index i covers range [i - (i & -i) + 1, i]. This hierarchical structure enables efficient prefix sum computation.

sections.title: Point Update
sections.content: Update value at index i. Add delta to all BIT indices that include i in their range. Move to next index: i += i & -i. Time: $O(\log n)$. Each update affects $O(\log n)$ indices.
sections.algorithm: while i <= n: bit[i] += delta; i += i & -i;

sections.title: Prefix Sum Query
sections.content: Query sum of elements from 1 to i. Sum BIT values for indices that contribute to prefix. Move to previous index: i -= i & -i. Time: $O(\log n)$. Each query accesses $O(\log n)$ indices.
sections.algorithm: sum = 0; while i > 0: sum += bit[i]; i -= i & -i; return sum;

sections.title: Range Sum Query
sections.content: Sum of elements from l to r = prefix_sum(r) - prefix_sum(l-1). Two prefix sum queries. Time: $O(\log n)$. BIT excels at prefix-based operations.

sections.title: BIT vs Segment Tree
sections.content: BIT: simpler code, less memory ($O(n)$ vs $O(4n)$), faster constant factor, limited to prefix-based operations. Segment Tree: more flexible (any range query, range updates, multiple operations), more complex, more memory. Choose BIT for prefix sums, segment tree for general range queries.

keyConcepts.name: Lowest Set Bit
keyConcepts.description: i & -i gives the lowest set bit of i. Determines the range covered by BIT index i. Key to BIT's structure.

keyConcepts.name: 1-Indexed
keyConcepts.description: BIT uses 1-indexed array. Index 0 is unused. This simplifies the lowest set bit calculation.

keyConcepts.name: Prefix to Range
keyConcepts.description: Range sum [l, r] = prefix(r) - prefix(l-1). BIT directly supports prefix, so range is derived.

keyConcepts.name: Inverse Operation
keyConcepts.description: Update moves forward (i += lsb), query moves backward (i -= lsb). These are inverse operations on the BIT structure.

steps.title: Initialize BIT
steps.description: Create BIT array of size n+1, initialized to 0.

steps.title: Build BIT
steps.description: For each element in original array, call update(i, arr[i]).
steps.code: for i in range(1, n+1): update(i, arr[i-1]);

steps.title: Point Update
steps.description: Add delta to index i. Update all affected BIT indices.
steps.code: while i <= n: bit[i] += delta; i += i & -i;

steps.title: Prefix Query
steps.description: Sum elements from 1 to i. Accumulate BIT values.
steps.code: sum = 0; while i > 0: sum += bit[i]; i -= i & -i; return sum;

steps.title: Range Query
steps.description: Sum elements from l to r using two prefix queries.

snippets.title: Fenwick Tree Implementation
Count Smaller After Self
snippets.code:
def count_smaller(nums):
    # Coordinate compression
    sorted_nums = sorted(set(nums))
    rank = {v: i+1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted_nums)}
    
    bit = FenwickTree(len(rank))
    result = [0] * len(nums)
    
    for i in range(len(nums)-1, -1, -1):
        r = rank[nums[i]]
        result[i] = bit.query(r - 1)  # Count smaller
        bit.update(r, 1)  # Add current
    
    return result
